about: C.22 tiered governance (Appendix E §3.1, §3.1.1; Appendix F Part 3). Every Mentor source file in a governed root belongs to exactly one component, and the component's tier says what automation may do to it. Read with docs/rebuild/mentor/SELF-IMPROVEMENT-GOVERNANCE-POLICY.md. Enforced by `npm run governance:check`. This file is itself Tier 1 (component governance.model).

tiers.tier_1: Never automate. Full human review and explicit sign-off by the Pedagogical Reviewer and the Safety/Trust Lead; never enters an automated path; every change needs a Tier 1 change-record row.
tiers.live_content_judging: Appendix E §3.1.1: live per-item content judging, its own axis beside the proposal tiers. Treated like Tier 1 for change control: floors may be tightened by a human, never loosened without full review; never changed by an automated pipeline.
tiers.tier_2: Gated automate. Micro-variants within approved bounds may be proposed automatically; release needs Stage 0, Stage 2 (simulated students), Stage 3 (a calibrated judge, C.23) or Stage 4 (human review), and Stage 5 (canary with a human reading real transcripts).
tiers.tier_3: Fully automate. Measurement and reporting whose output is information for a human; Stage 0 and instrumentation only.

components.title: The safety judge and the privacy boundary: whatever decides a conversation must be refused, paused, escalated or shown to a guardian, and what reaches the model about a child.
examples: Changing what the moderation judge refuses, or when it may be skipped
Changing the guardian review of memory notes
Adding a field the model sees about a child (the 14-field context contract)

components.title: The core evaluation rubric, its deterministic scorer and fixtures, every judge's instructions, the calibration standard and the seed and gold sets.
examples: Adding, removing or retargeting a rubric criterion
Editing the transcript judge's system prompt or a judge question
Lowering an agreement threshold, or editing the gold set's labels

components.title: The simulated-student suites that gate every change (Appendix F Stage 2) and the dialect/ASR bias audit (C.20). Weakening a gate is how an automated loop would hide a regression.
examples: Removing a simulated persona or relaxing what it must see
Changing a bias-audit fixture's expected outcome

components.title: The Block C non-negotiable constraints: no declared emotions, the hint ladder never repeats and honours 'just tell me', no mastery or remediation on one observation, the end-reason closing scripts, praise tied to a verifiable action, the check-in after a fired signal; and the controller and orchestrator that wire them.
examples: Letting mastery be declared on one observation
Changing the strategy-change ceiling (3 per minute)
Using the standard positive closing for a safety stop

components.title: Anything that could lengthen sessions or raise engagement as a side effect: the session budget and caps, the early-close signal, the paid-spend guard.
examples: Raising a session's soft or hard cap
Making the behavioural early-close signal fire later

components.title: The Stage 7 automatic rollbacks and the dashboard's regression thresholds (Tier-1-adjacent: tightened by a human at any time, never loosened without full review).
examples: Lowering the Default-to-Inaction kill-switch floor
Widening the answer-reveal ceiling or the disparity rule
Changing a Mentor kill-switch default or the C.10 corroboration floor in the Oracle configuration (oracle/src/env.ts)

components.title: This registry and the gates that enforce the tiers and the judge-calibration floors.
examples: Moving a component to a more autonomous tier
Widening a Tier 2 parameter's approved bounds
Declaring a new automated pipeline

components.title: The live-content author and judge, the content-risk lexicon, the sampling floors and suspension rules, and the curated-pack release contract (C.5, C.6).
examples: Editing the content judge's prompt (it also un-trusts the judge until recalibrated)
Lowering a sampling floor or the concordance floor

components.title: Prompt micro-variants, scripted and persona phrasing, hint and explanation wording, within the approved bounds.
examples: Rewording a scripted check-in line in one locale
A persona tone micro-variant tested in a canary

components.title: Pacing thresholds and signal weights the governance boundary names as proposable: telemetry weights, spaced-review horizons, dialogue calibration, alliance and disposition tuning, practice scheduling.
examples: Moving the telemetry latency z-score from 1.5 to 1.7
Renegotiating after 3 declines instead of 2

components.title: Runtime behaviour code with no governance rule of its own: grading, whiteboard, instruments, the turn schema, practice records.
examples: A whiteboard layout adjustment
A grading tolerance for spoken numbers

components.title: Measurement and reporting plumbing whose output is information for a human: the evaluation loop, the dashboard routes' data layer, the honesty-ledger records.
examples: Adding a breakdown to a report
Batching the evaluation pass differently

automatedPipelines.purpose: Merges Dependabot's patch-level Pulse image bumps after pulse CI passes.

decisions.summary: Adopts the three-tier model and the live-content axis (C.22) before any automated proposal-generation capability exists, with the initial classification above. Proposed in S06.14; binding on engineering from adoption, awaiting the two sign-offs.

OD-28 (owner review M-19): mixed Mentor files get finer Tier 1 boundaries at the level of top-level declarations. Oracle's controller.ts and orchestrator.ts and seven Core kill-switch modules are split: the strict component keeps every declaration by default ("*"), and the listed carve-outs move turn-pacing tables and two model-history windows to Tier 2 and report-only summaries and kill-switch log readers to Tier 3. Engineering's proposal; each carve-out takes effect only when both leads sign this decision, and until then the whole files stay Tier 1.
